az_5_queen_bee_area.blurb: A small cluster of boulders high in Middle Elden Canyon above Flagstaff, reached by a short off-trail scramble beyond the main canyon path. The ten problems here run from easy V2 up through a solid middle band of V6 and V7, with one standout hard line in the double digits. Expect crimpy, technical movement and a few rough landings, so pads and spotters matter. The setting is pleasant for the easier problems, which look out over town. It is best in warmer weather: the boulders catch morning sun and slide into canyon shade by late afternoon.

az_lockdown_rock.blurb: A compact winter sport crag on the lower slopes of Mount Lemmon near Tucson, with ten bolted lines on a wall roughly 30 to 50 feet tall. The wall runs from vertical to slightly overhanging. Grades start near 5.8, with a couple of 5.9s and 5.10s, then half the routes fall in the 5.11 range, so it suits climbers who want some moderate warm-up plus a handful of harder pitches. The face stays shaded until late morning and then takes sun for the rest of the day. The walk in is a roughly half-hour trek on a rough trail, and rock quality is mostly solid with a bit of loose stone left.

az_rivendell.blurb: A winter crag tucked up a streambed in Soldier's Canyon on the lower Catalina Highway, outside Tucson. Nine of its ten climbs are sport routes, with one aid line, and the grades sit mostly in the 5.8 to 5.10 range with a single 5.11. The wall is mostly vertical, faces west-northwest and picks up winter sun around midday. Many climbs begin on slightly water-polished rock before reaching good edges higher up. The long approach up the wash keeps crowds down and the setting is free of road noise, but expect a real hike with some brush and boulder scrambling to reach the base.
az_rivendell.parking_note: Pull off at the roadside spot just before the sharp hairpin curve on the Catalina Highway, a little over half a mile up from the start of the highway; the wash trail begins across the road.

az_snort_wall_the.blurb: A small face-climbing wall in Oak Creek Canyon between Flagstaff and Sedona, sitting just beneath the much larger Coke Wall. The ten routes here are a mix of bolted face lines and gear-protected pitches, spanning roughly 5.8 up to low 5.13, with most of them in the 5.10 to 5.12 band. Expect steep, slabby to overhanging walls of pocketed Coconino sandstone with sculpted features, particularly on the right side. The rock is sandy but holds together. Reaching it means crossing the creek and following the drainage to the cliff base, so it is a short adventure rather than a roadside crag.

az_backhand_wall.blurb: The best-known wall of the Hairpin Turn Area on the lower Catalina Highway near Tucson. Nine sport routes and one mixed line climb long, mostly vertical faces, with grades concentrated at 5.10 and a few at 5.11, and a single 5.8. The wall faces north and gets almost no sun, so it works on most days except the very coldest and hottest. Bolting is good, but the rock is somewhat loose, so climb carefully and have belayers wear helmets. The approach is a short climb up a boulder-strewn wash and then a trail around a corner, around 15 to 20 minutes.
az_backhand_wall.parking_note: Use the roadside pullout near mile marker 0.5 on the Catalina Highway, just before the sharp hairpin curve; cross the road and follow the wash uphill.

az_lost_world_at_jacks_canyon.blurb: A south-facing limestone cliff on the north side of Jacks Canyon, near Winslow, holding some of the tallest routes in the canyon at up to about 90 feet. Almost all of the ten climbs are bolted sport routes, with grades from an easy 5.5 through 5.9 and a cluster of 5.10s and 5.11s, plus one at 5.12. Because the cliff sits in full sun all day, it is a good choice on cold winter days when shadier walls stay chilly. Rock is generally good, though the middle section can feel crumbly. It is reached by its own dirt-road route, separate from the main canyon.

az_outpatient_clinic_the.blurb: The first crag you meet when hiking up the climbers trail from the Cave Springs area in Oak Creek Canyon, south of Sedona. Ten routes are spread out on both sides of the canyon, a mix of trad, sport and one aid line. Nearly all are hard: a lone 5.10, then four 5.11s and five 5.12s, so this is a place for strong leaders rather than beginners. The sandstone ranges from good to poor, and the canyon throws off a pleasant cool breeze. Routes are more scattered than at neighbouring sections of the canyon.

az_tiny_town.blurb: One of the top crags in Upper Middle Elden Canyon on Mount Elden above Flagstaff, at the far end of the cliff band past The Lair and The Hive. Ten short routes, nearly all sport with one trad line, range from a 5.9 to a 5.13, with most between 5.10 and 5.12. They are brief but punchy, with good movement and stone, and include some of the best warm-ups for the upper cliffs. It takes an adventurous hike of around 45 minutes from the trail easements, so wear approach shoes or sturdy boots and expect a quiet outing.
